version.changelog: The helper connects through Beatra's mainland network when your computer is in mainland China, and can open the approval page on Beatra's international site when you need another sign-in method.

llm.summary: The skill appears to make the advertised shift-handoff voice clips, but it also asks for broad reusable Beatra account authority and can silently update its own package files.

dimensions.detail: A remote authenticated service is expected for generated speech, and local token handling is documented with permission checks, but the shared full-scope ~/.beatra credential and package registration/route telemetry create a larger trust boundary than the narrow skill description suggests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package includes standard-looking authorization and uninstall helpers, but the bundled client silently checks for updates and installs newer package files by default without separate per-update confirmation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require user-visible planning and paid-stage confirmation, but all remote operations go through a bundled raw MCP client that can call arbitrary Beatra tool names using the broad shared credential.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a reusable Beatra device token, installation inventory, network/update state, and default-on auto-update settings under ~/.beatra; uninstall is bounded and disclosed, but the persistent privilege is high impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Voice generation, cloning, uploads, task polling, and wallet checks fit the stated purpose, but scripts/authorize.py requests broad scopes including image, video, music, artifact read/write, wallet spending, voice management, task read, and task cancel authority beyond a shift-handoff voice workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust Beatra with a reusable device authorization that can do more than this one voice workflow. Consider disabling automatic updates with the documented command, keeping limited account balance, and revoking the device authorization from the Beatra Console when finished.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifact really requests broad media, artifact, wallet, voice, and task scopes that exceed the advertised shift-handoff voice use case.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: voice and task operations are partly purpose-aligned, but broad artifact/task authority and default-on self-update are materially overbroad for this skill.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded from credential-theft framing: the credential file is documented, permission-checked, and used for Beatra authentication, but the shared full-scope token remains a Review concern.
[TP4] expected: Mostly downgraded: uninstall and disconnect instructions are disclosed lifecycle behavior, and the uninstall script avoids deleting shared state unless this is the last Beatra skill.
[RA1] unexpected: Accepted: scripts/mcp_client.py implements self-update that can replace package-owned files, and the skill enables silent automatic updates by default.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in part: the manifest does not provide a narrow permission allowlist despite requiring shell execution, network access, local files, uploads, and authenticated MCP calls.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: automatic updates are documented and include checksum and path checks, but they still change executable behavior without a fresh user decision.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: region routing is disclosed, uses fixed Beatra hosts, and has user controls; it is not by itself a deceptive routing flow.
